title: Culture Minister Urtasun Presses Vivas to 'Speed Up' Transfer of 500 Ceuta Minors to Mainland
detail: Culture Minister Ernest Urtasun publicly urged Ceuta president Juan Jesús Vivas to 'agilice' (speed up) the mainland transfer of 500 unaccompanied minors that Youth and Childhood Minister Sira Rego had proposed, saying 'necesitamos su colaboración' (we need your cooperation) and calling the relocations 'absolutely necessary' as 'a matter of humanity.' Urtasun said an administrative process still has to be completed on Ceuta's end and cited precedents from Lampedusa and the Greek islands, while accusing the PP of an 'absolute lack of solidarity' since no PP-run autonomous community has offered placements. Separately, Ceuta's government published a cost schedule for minor transfers — €50 by boat, €21 per taxi kilometre, €25 per half-hour of flight time — and had allocated up to €200,000 for the transfers.

media.caption: Culture Minister Ernest Urtasun calls on Ceuta president Vivas to speed up minor transfers

title: Vox Brings Congress Motion Demanding Immediate Expulsions and Halt to Minor Transfers
detail: Vox brought a motion to the full Congress floor, arising from an urgent question to Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres, demanding: immediate expulsion of irregular migrants, a halt to the distribution of unaccompanied minors across Spain's regions, suspension of the Spain-Morocco Treaty of Friendship, Good Neighbourliness and Cooperation, an audit of the crisis's extraordinary costs, a reciprocity-based review of bilateral relations, and reinforced Armed Forces and security personnel in Ceuta and Melilla. The party's text described the Jul 30-31 crossing as an 'invasion,' and cited 37 sexual-assault cases filed in Ceuta courts between Jul 30 and Sep 14 involving men who entered irregularly. The PP's position on the motion remained undecided ahead of the vote.

media.caption: Vox leader Santiago Abascal, whose party brought the Ceuta motion to Congress
